assumptions.chosen: Exactly as the recorded decision record and its owner summary already define it: the count n is the number of residual items in the decision record recorded for that acceptance decision (the decision-record artifact the decision references) whose kind is not "should" (unverified should-criteria) and not "advisory_constraint" (advisory constraints); "Nothing is accepted without proof" is shown when n is 0 (the record's attention is "clean"). This matches the wording "N item(s) would be accepted without proof" / "Nothing is accepted without proof" of the explanation the control loop already writes for the same decision, so the two never contradict each other on the page. The text is "1 item would be accepted without proof" for n = 1 and "{n} items would be accepted without proof" for n >= 2.
assumptions.question: Which recorded items count as "items that would be accepted without proof", and when does the page say "Nothing is accepted without proof"?

assumptions.chosen: Only to open acceptance decisions, since "Decisions of other kinds are unchanged". The acceptance list item contains exactly one link to /tasks/{id} of its task, whose visible text is "{task key} · {task title}" (the format the batch card on /decisions already uses), e.g. "T4 · Demo: share a list".
assumptions.question: Does "Each decision links to its task by the task key and title" apply to every open decision or only to acceptance decisions, and what is the link's text?

assumptions.chosen: Like the other preview demo data (APP_ENV=preview only, idempotent, also on a preview database seeded earlier), the Demo Project gains two demo tasks in state DONE, each with one open acceptance decision whose recorded context references a stored decision-record artifact: T4 "Demo: share a list" (decision title "Accept T4: Demo: share a list"), whose recorded decision record has attention "review" and three residual items - two counted ones (kinds such as "finding" and "verifier") and one of kind "should" - so the page shows "2 items would be accepted without proof"; and T5 "Demo: book covers" (decision title "Accept T5: Demo: book covers"), whose recorded decision record has attention "clean" and exactly one residual item of kind "should", so the page shows "Nothing is accepted without proof". The explanation (why) of each demo decision is worded as the control loop's owner summary would word it for that record. Nothing else of the demo data changes.
assumptions.question: What demonstration data does the gate preview carry so the feature can be checked?

interface.ui: Sign-in for the gate preview: GET /auth/preview (redirects to / with an owner session). Decisions page: route /decisions, h1 "Decisions", card header "Open", one list item per open decision (unchanged for every kind except acceptance). Kind label of an acceptance decision on /decisions: "Acceptance" (unchanged); other kind labels unchanged: "Contract review", "Confirm on GitHub", "Decision", "Budget". NEW in each open acceptance list item: (1) exactly one link to /tasks/{id} of its task whose visible text is "{task key} · {task title}" (e.g. "T4 · Demo: share a list"); (2) one element whose whole visible text (surrounding whitespace removed) is exactly one of: "1 item would be accepted without proof", "{n} items would be accepted without proof" (n >= 2, decimal digits), or "Nothing is accepted without proof"; when the acceptance decision has no recorded decision record, neither statement is shown. The acceptance list item also keeps the kind label, the line "{project} · {task key} · {age}", the decision title (shortened per T0) and the explanation text, and contains no button, form, text input or select. Task page: route /tasks/{id}, page title "Task · Agents". Preview demo data (A3): Demo Project task T4 "Demo: share a list" with the open acceptance decision "Accept T4: Demo: share a list" -> "2 items would be accepted without proof"; task T5 "Demo: book covers" with the open acceptance decision "Accept T5: Demo: book covers" -> "Nothing is accepted without proof"; existing demo decisions of T1 ("Contract review", "Approve the contract for T1: Demo: export a list as CSV") and T2 ("Decision") unchanged.

non_goals: Changing list items of open decisions of any kind other than acceptance on /decisions, the batch card "{n} contracts ready in {project}", or the open-decision strip of the Command page (/).

Listing the individual residual items (their texts, kinds or ids), the basis, blockers, readiness, package hash or decision-record hash on the Decisions page; the task page already lists the residual and keeps doing so unchanged.

Changing how decision records are computed, stored or hashed (decide, ownerSummary, the decision-record artifact, the acceptance decision's recorded context), the evidence package, the gate, the Verifier or the control loop.
Any new button, form, action, filter, sort order or API endpoint (including under /api/v0); approving, rejecting or re-computing anything from the Decisions page.
Changing the database schema or migrations.
Showing the count on the Command page, project pages, the task page or the System page.
Making the Decisions page fit a phone-width screen beyond what it does today.

scope.summary: On the Decisions page (/decisions), in the "Open" card, each open acceptance decision (kind label "Acceptance") additionally shows, read from the decision record recorded for that decision, how many items would be accepted without proof ("{n} items would be accepted without proof", singular "1 item would be accepted without proof"), or "Nothing is accepted without proof" when there are none, and links to its task with a link whose text is the task key and the task title ("{key} · {title}"). The list item stays read-only and shows only recorded facts: nothing is computed beyond counting the recorded residual items, nothing is written, and an acceptance decision without a recorded decision record shows neither statement. Open decisions of other kinds (contract review, confirm on GitHub, decision, budget) are listed exactly as before. The gate preview's demonstration data gains two demo tasks with open acceptance decisions and recorded decision records so the feature can be checked black-box; all earlier demo data stays as it is.
